senses.sense_definition: Moving or tending to move away from a center or axis.

examples.text: The clothes dry quickly because the spinning drum creates strong <w>centrifugal</w> force.
As the car took the sharp turn, <w>centrifugal</w> force pushed the passengers toward the outer door.

senses.sense_definition: Developing or opening outward from the center, especially describing flower clusters that mature from the summit downward.

examples.text: Botanists noted the <w>centrifugal</w> flowering pattern where the central buds bloomed first.
This plant species exhibits a distinctive <w>centrifugal</w> inflorescence throughout the spring.

senses.sense_definition: Having the radicle directed toward the periphery or side of the seed or fruit.

examples.text: Under the microscope, the plant embryo displays a clearly <w>centrifugal</w> orientation.
The seed exhibits a <w>centrifugal</w> radicle turned outward against the pericarp wall.

senses.sense_definition: A rotating machine used in sugar refining to separate crystals from molasses.

examples.text: Workers loaded the warm mixture directly into the industrial <w>centrifugals</w>.
A modern <w>centrifugal</w> separates sugar crystals rapidly during the refining process.
